;Armed conflict and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**A [[car bomb]] in [[Turkey|Turkish]]-controlled [[Suluk, Syria|Suluk]], [[Tell Abyad District]], [[Raqqa Governorate]], kills five people and wounds others. Turkey's [[Ministry of National Defense (Turkey) |defense ministry]] says the attack killed eight civilians and was by the [[Kurdistan Workers' Party|PKK]]/[[People's Protection Units|YPG]] group. [https://www.trtworld.com/middle-east/car-bomb-kills-eight-civilians-in-northern-syria-turkey-32421 (TRTWorld)]
**The [[United Kingdom|UK]]-based [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights|SOHR]] says an [[Israeli Armed Forces|Israeli]] missile attack near [[Damascus]] killed three foreigners, believed to be [[Iranian peoples|Iranians]]. [https://www.ynetnews.com/article/B1r5AAaCH (Ynetnews)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[The Pentagon]] says a [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. soldier]] has been [[Killed in action|killed in combat]]. The [[Taliban]] claim a [[Improvised explosive device|roadside bomb]] in [[Char Dara District]], [[Kunduz Province]] was responsible. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/afghanistan-american-service-member-killed-us-military-says-today-2019-12-23/ (CBS News)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)]], [[Operation Barkhane]]
**[[France]]'s [[Ministry of Armed Forces (France)|defense ministry]] reports its first [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|armed drone]] strike. On Saturday, a [[General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper|Reaper]] [[drone strike]] killed seven in central [[Mali]]. [https://www.dailystar.com.lb/News/World/2019/Dec-23/498009-france-says-it-carries-out-1st-armed-drone-strike-in-mali.ashx (AP via ''The Daily Star'')]
*[[2019 Iranian protests]]
**Unknown [[Government of Iran|Iranian]] officials claimed the death toll is 1,500 in recent crackdowns by security forces. The United States confirmed the report, including the deaths of 400 women and a dozen teenagers. [https://www.voanews.com/middle-east/voa-news-iran/us-confirms-report-citing-iran-officials-saying-1500-killed-protests (VOA)]

;Business and economy
*[[Crimean Bridge]]
**A [[rail transport|railway]] bridge over the [[Kerch Strait]] connecting [[Russia]] and [[Crimea]], the [[List of longest bridges|longest]] in Europe, is inaugurated. [https://apnews.com/6123f7874d16f3819965dbc00f20e850 (AP)]
*The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] launches an investigation into allegations of money laundering at the [[state-owned]] mining company [[Gécamines]], relating to a [[Euro|€]]200 million loan by the sanctioned [[Dan Gertler#Fleurette Group and Fleurette Properties, 2006|Fleurette Group]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-mining/congo-prosecutors-probe-israeli-billionaires-loan-to-state-mining-company-idUSKBN1YR1JK?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Aftermath of the [[Boeing 737 MAX groundings]]
**[[Boeing]] announces the resignation of its [[CEO]], [[Dennis Muilenburg]], amidst ongoing controversy over the crashes and subsequent groundings of the [[Boeing 737 MAX]] fleet. [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/12/23/business/boeing-dennis-muilenburg/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Economy of China]]
**[[China]] announces the reduction of [[tariff]]s on 850 products and measures to [[open market]]s in several industries. [https://apnews.com/a3c6388217bfc1a48267fbb763608316 (AP)]

;Health and environment
*[[Fukushima disaster cleanup]]
**[[Japan]]'s [[Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry]] proposes gradually releasing or allowing to evaporate massive amounts of [[Radioactive decay|radioactive]] water at the [[tsunami]]-hit [[Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant]]. [https://time.com/5754524/fukushima-nuclear-water-release-environment/ (''TIME'')]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–United States relations]], [[Korean peace process]]
**[[North Korea]] warns of a "[[Christmas]] gift" if the [[United States]] does not come up with an agreement by the end of the year. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/dec/12/us-warns-north-korea-of-consequences-of-missile-test-christmas-gift (''The Guardian'')]  

;Law and crime
*[[Assassination of Jamal Khashoggi]]
**A court in [[Saudi Arabia]] sentences five people to death for the 2018 killing of [[journalist]] [[Jamal Khashoggi]]. Three other defendants are given prison sentences totalling a combined 24 years, and another three are acquitted. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-50890633 (BBC News)]
**The [[United Nations]] rapporteur on [[summary execution]]s, [[Agnès Callamard]], describes the sentence as a "mockery" of justice, since, according to her, it was an "[[extrajudicial killing|extrajudicial execution]] for which the state of Saudi Arabia is responsible" and its masterminds walk free. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/turkey-rights-groups-decry-saudi-verdict-khashoggi-murder-191223171239748.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Algerian protests]]
**The [[Chief of Staff of the People's National Army]] of [[Algeria]], [[Ahmed Gaid Salah]], dies unexpectedly of a [[heart attack]]. [[Saïd Chengriha]] is appointed to the post ''ad interim''. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1602921/middle-east (AP via ''Arab News'')]
*[[2019 Jharkhand Legislative Assembly election]]
**In an election occurring in the midst of [[Citizenship Amendment Act protests|massive protests against the central government]],  the incumbent right-wing [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] is projected to lose its majority to the [[United Progressive Alliance]] parties in the eastern [[India]]n [[States and union territories of India|state]] of [[Jharkhand]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/12/india-bjp-concedes-defeat-jharkhand-state-assembly-election-191223121238135.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2019 French pension reform strike]]
**Around 30 protestors clash with [[riot police]] at the [[Gare de Lyon]] in [[Paris]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-france-protests-pensions/protesters-clash-with-police-at-key-paris-rail-terminal-idUSKBN1YR123?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Politics of Bosnia and Herzegovina]]
**The [[Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnian]] [[Parliamentary Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina|parliament]] approves [[Chairman of the Council of Ministers of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Prime Minister]] [[Zoran Tegeltija]]'s cabinet after a 14-month deadlock, caused by disagreements over proceeding with [[Accession of Bosnia and Herzegovina to NATO|NATO integration]], with Tegeltija stating his main priority is pursuing [[Accession of Bosnia and Herzegovina to the European Union|membership with the European Union]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bosnia-government/bosnian-lawmakers-approve-new-government-after-14-month-deadlock-idUSKBN1YR1JE?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Politics of Romania]]
**Centrist [[Florin Cîțu]] is approved by the [[Parliament of Romania|Parliament]] as the new [[Prime Minister]], succeeding acting [[Nicolae Ciucă]]. [https://news.yahoo.com/romanias-parliament-approves-government-171428082.html (Yahoo! News)]
